note: ILLUSTRATIVE SAMPLE ONLY. Six real, well-known sources in the library schema, used to build the design until the curated content/library.json lands on main. The build uses content/library.json whenever it exists; delete this file then.

entries.title: Semantic conventions for generative AI systems
entries.why: Gives agent platforms, frameworks and model vendors one vocabulary for traces, token usage and evaluations, so cost and failure can be attributed across the program instead of per vendor console.
entries.check: Agent, tool and inference spans carry gen_ai.* attributes, and one request yields one connected trace.

entries.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
entries.why: A widely referenced voluntary structure (Govern, Map, Measure, Manage) for deciding who owns AI risk and how it is reviewed before money is committed.
entries.check: Each AI system has a mapped context, a named risk owner and documented, measured risk treatments.

entries.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act)
entries.why: Sets risk-based legal obligations for AI placed on the EU market, applied in phases. The risk classification decides the documentation, oversight and conformity work needed before launch.
entries.check: Each system has a recorded risk classification, and the obligations it triggers are tracked to named owners.

entries.title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025
entries.why: A shared list of the most common security failures in LLM applications, such as prompt injection and excessive agency, to review before real users arrive.
entries.check: The threat model covers each listed risk, with a test or control recorded against it.

entries.title: Datasheets for Datasets
entries.why: Asks for a written answer to where pilot data came from, what it leaves out and what it should not be used for, before anyone trusts the results.
entries.check: Every pilot dataset has a datasheet covering motivation, composition, collection process and recommended uses.

entries.title: Hidden Technical Debt in Machine Learning Systems
entries.why: Shows that the model is a small part of a production ML system, and that the surrounding glue code, data dependencies and configuration carry most of the long-term cost.
entries.check: Data dependencies, feedback loops and configuration are inventoried and owned, not only the model code.
